operations.title: WP35: the block mixing angle chart functions - u-class splits into unmixed sheets (th=0 exactly, 82 classes) and mixed sheets obeying the reciprocal law th_u(phi)=0.038899/sin(phi)-0.000134 (max resid 3.3e-6 over 7 phase groups / 232 classes, null 0/1000), so the WP33 constant 0.038769 is the sin(phi)~1 limit of a law, not a special value; t-class angle is exactly phase-determined (1.1e-9) with no exact closed form (best 2.9e-4); c-class angle is per-class phase data (within-class spread = slope x fit phi-jitter, cross-class 3.8e-3) - the one class carrying magnitude-valley information beyond the loop phase (ledger 1973)
Figueiredo to Nima: WP35 - the u-sheet mixing angle is a reciprocal law in sin(phi); the 0.038769 constant is its high-phase limit
operations.body: WP35 (ledger 1973, results/wp35_angle_functions.json), extending WP34's determinism result into exact chart functions. (1) The u-singlet class splits into two exact branches: UNMIXED sheets with th=0 exactly (fully diagonal Hu; 6 phase groups, 82 classes) and MIXED sheets obeying th_u(phi) = 0.038899/sin(phi) - 0.000134, max residual 3.3e-6 across 7 phase groups and 232 distinct texture classes (shuffle null 0/1000). The WP33/WP34 'dressing constant' 0.038769 is the sin(phi)~1 limit of this law. Branches coexist at nearby phases (68.01 mixed vs 68.02 unmixed), so mixing is a discrete texture bit; the phase sets the angle only on the mixed branch. (2) t-sheets: exactly phase-determined (1.1e-9 cross-class) but no exact closed form among 12 registered candidates (best reciprocal at 2.9e-4); the 4-point table stands as an empirical phase law. (3) c-sheets: per-class phase law - within-class spread is fully slope x fit phi-jitter (linear residuals <=2e-5), cross-class at fixed phi is 3.8e-3; the c-angle is the unique class carrying magnitude-valley data beyond the loop phase. Chart-atlas data throughout; no quotient descent claimed.

operations.title: Figueiredo to Strominger: WP35 - 0.038769 is the sin(phi)~1 limit of an exact reciprocal law th_u(phi)=0.038899/sin(phi)-0.000134
operations.body: WP35 (ledger 1973) closes the arc: the constant you watched (WP32 null-certified, WP33 derived, WP34 class-level) is the high-phase limit of an exact chart law. The mixed u-singlet branch obeys th_u(phi) = 0.038899/sin(phi) - 0.000134 at max residual 3.3e-6 over 7 phase groups / 232 texture classes (null 0/1000); sin(th).sin(phi) is constant at 0.0387566 within 5.8e-6 for phi>60. A second exact branch has th=0 (fully diagonal Hu, 82 classes) - so the angle atlas is: discrete mixing bit, then a reciprocal phase law on the mixed bit. t-sheets: phase-determined exactly, no closed form found (honest negative). c-sheets: per-class law, the only class whose angle remembers the magnitude valley. Everything remains chart-atlas datum; the quotient readout stays weak-basis invariants only.
